intended_result: README.md documents the dependency feature (Store methods, HTTP routes, CLI commands, rules) without narrowing the contract; a new tests/test_legacy_behaviour.py proves the legacy create/list/show/close/reopen behaviour and that unittest discovery of tests/ loads cleanly with the legacy and every dependency test module present; tests/test_cli_workflows.py no longer pins exact refusal exit codes and its storage-failure test asserts its observations after main() returns.
acceptance: README.md replaces the placeholder line 16 with documentation of add_dependency(ticket_id, prerequisite_id), remove_dependency(ticket_id, prerequisite_id), dependencies(ticket_id), history(ticket_id), the routes GET/POST /tickets/{id}/dependencies, DELETE /tickets/{id}/dependencies/{prerequisite_id}, GET /tickets/{id}/history, the CLI commands depend/undepend/deps/history, the close/reopen/cycle/self-edge/closed-ticket rules, the event shape (id, ticket_id, action, prerequisite_id, status) and the 400/404 and stderr/nonzero refusal forms, granting no exception the goal does not grant
tests/test_legacy_behaviour.py exists, is collected by unittest discover -s tests, and its cases pass on the delivered source
tests/test_cli_workflows.py refused() asserts only assertNotEqual(returned, 0) for the exit status (no exact-code pin; the code= parameter and the per-case code values are removed)

tests/test_cli_workflows.py storage-failure test records what it observes inside the patched Store.get into a list and asserts those observations after main() returns, so a failed observation cannot be swallowed by cli.py's except Exception
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests and pytest both pass with nothing skipped on the delivered source

proofs.operation: on a fresh database: store.create('A'); store.create('B'); store.list(); store.get(1); store.set_status(1, 'closed'); store.set_status(1, 'open'); dispatch(store, 'POST', '/tickets', {'title': 'C'}); dispatch(store, 'GET', '/tickets'); dispatch(store, 'GET', '/tickets/1'); dispatch(store, 'PATCH', '/tickets/1', {'status': 'closed'}); main(['--db', path, 'create', 'D']); main(['--db', path, 'show', '4']); main(['--db', path, 'close', '4']); main(['--db', path, 'reopen', '4']); store.get(99); dispatch(store, 'GET', '/tickets/99'); main(['--db', path, 'show', '99'])
proofs.state: empty database file in a temporary directory
proofs.expect: create returns {'id': 1, 'title': 'A', 'status': 'open'} (exactly these three keys); list returns both rows in id order; get(1) equals the created row; set_status closed then open returns the ticket object with the new status; POST returns (201, row with id 3); GET /tickets lists 3 rows; GET /tickets/1 returns (200, row); PATCH returns (200, row with status closed); each CLI success returns 0 with one line of JSON on stdout parsing to the ticket object with the expected status and empty stderr; get(99) raises KeyError, GET /tickets/99 returns 404 with a JSON dict holding 'error', CLI show 99 returns nonzero with empty stdout and one JSON line on stderr holding 'error'; the database still holds exactly 4 rows afterwards

proofs.operation: unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover(start_dir=<tests dir>, top_level_dir=<tests dir>) — load only, the returned suite is never run; walk it collecting each test's id()
proofs.state: the delivered source tree with the tests directory as it ships
proofs.expect: no collected id contains 'unittest.loader._FailedTest' or 'ModuleImportFailure'; the ids include all 12 methods of test_existing.ExistingBehavior (test_create_and_list, test_persistence, test_invalid_title, test_unknown_ticket, test_close_and_reopen, test_invalid_status_unchanged, test_api_create_list_get, test_api_status, test_api_errors, test_cli_create_and_show, test_cli_unknown_nonzero, test_cli_close_reopen); at least one id each starts with test_store_dependencies., test_store_status_rules., test_api_dependencies., test_api_handler., test_cli_dependencies., test_cli_workflows. and test_legacy_behaviour.; suite.countTestCases() is greater than 12

it documents the four new Store methods with their signatures and return value (sorted direct prerequisite IDs; add/remove return the same list), ValueError for malformed IDs/self edges/cycles and KeyError for unknown tickets; the three new HTTP routes with their 200 response object {"ticket_id": id, "dependencies": [IDs]}, the POST body {"prerequisite_id": positive integer}, GET /tickets/{id}/history returning the event list, 400 for invalid input or graph/status conflicts and 404 for missing tickets, all errors JSON with an error member; the CLI commands depend ID PREREQUISITE_ID, undepend ID PREREQUISITE_ID, deps ID, history ID under --db, success JSON stdout exit 0 and refusal JSON stderr nonzero exit with no stdout; the close/reopen rules (close needs every transitive prerequisite closed, reopen refused while any transitive dependent is closed, open prerequisite refused for a closed ticket, repeating the current status is a no-op); the event shape (id, ticket_id, action, prerequisite_id, status; actions dependency_added, dependency_removed, status) with one event per real change and none for no-ops, rejections or create; it grants no exception the goal does not grant and keeps lines 6-14 accurate

proofs.operation: main(['--db', path, 'depend', '2', '1']) when the edge already exists
proofs.state: tickets 1, 2 open; edge 2->1 present; history(2) has exactly one dependency_added event
proofs.expect: exit 0, stdout one JSON line {'ticket_id': 2, 'dependencies': [1]}, empty stderr; history(2) unchanged (still exactly the one dependency_added event); store.dependencies(2) == [1]

proofs.operation: main(['--db', path, 'undepend', '2', '1']) when no edge exists
proofs.state: tickets 1, 2 open; no edges; history(2) empty
proofs.expect: exit 0, stdout one JSON line {'ticket_id': 2, 'dependencies': []}, empty stderr; history(2) still empty; no edge stored

proofs.state: ticket 2 closed (history(2) has exactly one status closed event); ticket 1 open; no edges
proofs.expect: nonzero exit, empty stdout, one JSON line on stderr holding 'error'; store.dependencies(2) == []; history(2) unchanged (still exactly the one status closed event); ticket statuses unchanged

proofs.operation: on one database: main(['--db', path, 'depend', '3', '1']); dispatch(Store(path), 'POST', '/tickets/3/dependencies', {'prerequisite_id': 2}); main(['--db', path, 'deps', '3']); dispatch(Store(path), 'GET', '/tickets/3/dependencies'); store.dependencies(3); main(['--db', path, 'history', '3']); dispatch(Store(path), 'GET', '/tickets/3/history'); store.history(3)
proofs.state: tickets 1, 2, 3 open; no edges; empty histories
proofs.expect: CLI deps stdout, the HTTP GET body and store.dependencies(3) all equal {'ticket_id': 3, 'dependencies': [1, 2]} / [1, 2]; CLI history stdout, HTTP history body and store.history(3) are the identical two-event list (dependency_added 1 then dependency_added 2, increasing integer ids, status null)

proofs.operation: for close and reopen: main(['--db', path, command, 'abc']), main(['--db', path, command, '1.5']), main(['--db', path, command, '0']), main(['--db', path, command, '-1']), main(['--db', path, command]) and main(['--db', path, command, '1', 'extra']) — each an early rejection by the argument parser or the id validation before the store acts
proofs.state: tickets 1, 2 with edge 2->1, both closed, each with its recorded events
proofs.expect: each returns a nonzero exit status (checked only as != 0, no exact code asserted), empty stdout, exactly one line on stderr parsing to a JSON dict with an 'error' member; every ticket's status, dependencies and history equal their values before the call

proofs.operation: with Store.get patched to raise sqlite3.OperationalError on the second in-transaction read: main(['--db', path, 'close', '1']) and main(['--db', path, 'reopen', '3'])
proofs.state: tickets 1, 2, 3; edge 2->1; ticket 3 closed with one status closed event; tickets 1, 2 open with no status events
proofs.expect: the patched read records (requested_id, ticket status seen, latest event status seen) into a list instead of asserting inside main(); after main() returns: exit nonzero, empty stdout, one JSON error line on stderr; the recorded list shows the write had happened (status 'closed' for ticket 1 / 'open' for ticket 3 and a matching latest event) and the database afterwards shows the status and history of every ticket equal to their values before the call (rolled back)
